complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Notion 클라이언트 래퍼 및 타입 정의
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) Create singleton client wrapper in src/lib/notion/client.ts with Korean comments, (2) Define ResumeProject type with all required fields (id, slug, title, category, tags, status, publishedDate, lastEditedTime, blocks), (3) Create NotionBlock discriminated union for all supported block types, (4) Define RichTextSpan type for text annotations, (5) Create NotionBlockType enum. Ensure TypeScript strict mode compatibility and proper type narrowing support for discriminated unions.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity due to TypeScript type system requirements. The codebase already has a strong TypeScript foundation (src/lib/types/index.ts exists with well-structured types). This task requires creating a new type hierarchy for Notion data models with discriminated unions, which needs careful design for type safety. The singleton pattern is straightforward, but the type definitions need to be comprehensive to support all subsequent tasks. No external integrations at this stage reduces risk.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Decompose into: (1) Implement queryDatabase with filter/sort parameters, (2) Handle Category/Status filtering logic, (3) Implement recursive getPageContent with pagination (has_more handling), (4) Create getPageMetadata for property extraction, (5) Integrate unstable_cache with proper tag structure, (6) Implement rate limit error handling with Korean messages, (7) Add recursive block children fetching with depth limit (max 3), (8) Write comprehensive error handling for all Notion API failure modes (network, auth, 429, malformed responses). Consider using a retry mechanism for rate limits.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to multiple integration points: Notion API pagination, recursive block fetching, Next.js caching layer (unstable_cache), rate limiting, and error handling. The PRD specifies handling 100+ blocks with pagination, which requires careful state management. Rate limit 429 handling needs queue logic. The caching strategy with tags (notion-db, notion-page-{id}) requires understanding Next.js 15+ cache invalidation patterns. Recursive depth limiting adds algorithmic complexity. This is the foundation for all data operations, making it critical path work.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: BlockNote 에디터 통합 및 본문 편집 구현
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) Install and configure BlockNote packages (@blocknote/core, @blocknote/react), (2) Create BlockNoteEditor.tsx client component with custom schema (paragraph/heading/list/code/image only), (3) Build notionToBlockNote converter in block-converter.ts, (4) Build blockNoteToNotion converter with discriminated union handling, (5) Integrate Tailwind v4 theme into editor styles, (6) Implement dark mode support using globals.css .dark class, (7) Add editor change tracking (dirty state), (8) Handle image URL input (temporary, no upload), (9) Update Task 7 page to replace preview with editor. Ensure type safety across conversion boundaries.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to schema mapping between two different systems. BlockNote has its own type system that must be bidirectionally mapped to Notion's block structure. The codebase uses Tailwind v4 with custom CSS variables (@theme inline in globals.css), which may conflict with BlockNote's default styles. Dark mode requires careful integration (ThemeProvider uses next-themes with attribute='class'). Type-safe converters with discriminated unions are algorithmically complex. Risk: BlockNote may not support all Notion block nuances, requiring workarounds. Performance concerns with large documents (100+ blocks). The existing form patterns help, but this introduces a new third-party editor with its own API surface.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Write-back 구현 - 속성 및 본문 저장 Server Actions
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Decompose into: (1) Create updateProjectMetadata Server Action with pages.update API, (2) Implement optimistic locking conflict check using lastEditedTime, (3) Build deleteAllChildren helper with proper error handling, (4) Create appendChildrenInBatches with 100-block batching and rate limit queuing (200ms delay), (5) Implement snapshot-based rollback mechanism, (6) Add revalidateTag for cache invalidation (notion-page-${pageId}), (7) Integrate Server Actions into Task 8 save button with useTransition, (8) Add loading states and Korean toast messages (success/failure/conflict), (9) Implement Zod validation for all Server Action inputs, (10) Build conflict warning UI banner. Test extensively with concurrent edits and network failures.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Very high complexity - this is the most critical and risky task. It involves: transactional semantics (delete-all → append with rollback), distributed conflict detection (optimistic locking via lastEditedTime), rate limiting with queuing, batch processing (100 blocks), Next.js cache invalidation, and error recovery. The PRD specifies a delete-all-children → append strategy, which is destructive and requires atomic-like behavior (hence snapshot rollback). Rate limit handling (429 responses) needs a queue with delays. Conflict detection requires comparing timestamps, with UX for informing users of stale edits. Server Actions are async, requiring proper useTransition integration for pending states. This task has the highest potential for data loss if not implemented correctly. Extensive testing needed (edge cases: partial failures, network timeouts, concurrent edits).
